prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot to Shore Control Room for export reviews), Main Transformer (loading vs limits), export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory when capability<dispatch target; applies accepted ceiling, records time). Public grid, port out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; follows validated commands; blocks protection conflicts; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms to Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, station service transformers, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace). Substation Operator: authorized switching, clearances; Substation Degraded mode on alarm loss; records Grid Constraint mode. Grid Dispatcher: targets/ramps. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): instruction history, assigns vessel/crew. Alarms safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; Session Revocation Receipt to Cybersecurity Gateway; records security access/control events), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; holds last validated limit on grid comms loss; operational view of affected systems, coordinates protective actions), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale), Operations Radio Console, Work Permit Portal, Personnel Tracking Console. Weather Service, Metocean Buoy, Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record). Modes: Weather Hold, Vessel Standby. Vessel Master: Transfer Manifest Addendum, Crew Count Correction, records transit crew changes, onboard count. North/South Access Scanner. Marine Coordinator: capacity, Vessel AIS Receiver, reviews return movements, receives escalations. Personnel accounted before vessel-to-structure transfer; report arrival/departure; reconciled vs return roster at shore. Field Supervisor confirms work party complete, escalates absences/overdue check-ins. HSE Officer scheduled checks. Comms loss: local record, report later. Records: time, location, role, disposition. Cyber: Cybersecurity Gateway monitors external traffic; continuous monitoring (logins, config changes, off-window comms); Cybersecurity Analyst escalates to on-duty operations lead. Role-based access; Control Engineer, SCADA Engineer individual accounts; privileged access recorded; periodic

New part:
S428: Cybersecurity Analyst produces the Firmware Hash Attestation for controlled software releases.
S429: Field Supervisor checks that cybersecurity requirements are included in the work briefing before technicians begin affected tasks.
S430: Field Supervisor uses the Deferred Task Rationale when a cybersecurity-related work item must be postponed.
S431: Personnel report suspected compromise, lost credentials, and unexplained equipment behavior promptly through the established operations channel.
S432: The incident lead classifies each report, assigns an owner, and records its time, scope, and current status.
S433: When containment is needed, technical teams isolate only the affected connection or service where this can be done without creating an unsafe operating condition.
S434: The Control Engineer and Electrical Technician coordinate any operational changes with the relevant duty role before implementation.
S435: The Cybersecurity Analyst preserves relevant logs and technical evidence while limiting access to personnel assigned to the investigation.
S436: Recovery begins only after the incident lead confirms that the threat is contained and the affected system is suitable for return to service.
S437: The SCADA Engineer validates restored configurations and communications before normal monitoring responsibilities resume.
S438: Material actions and decisions are documented with the time, location, responsible role, and disposition.
S439: After significant incidents, the technical teams review causes, response effectiveness, and corrective actions with operations management.
S440: Blade inspection is initiated when scheduled surveillance, turbine alarms, or operational reports indicate that blade condition requires review.
S441: The Maintenance Planning Engine combines inspection intervals, prior defect history, and turbine availability to propose survey dates.
S442: The Duty Planner confirms the inspection priority and coordinates access with the Marine Coordinator or the Field Supervisor.
S443: The Weather Service and Metocean Buoy provide forecasts and measured conditions for assessing whether remote or close-access work is safe.
S444: Remote surveys use the Blade Inspection Drone to capture repeatable views of blade surfaces while the turbine is in an approved operating state.
S445: The Blade Specialist reviews the tile image to classify visible damage and identify areas requiring closer assessment.
S446: Image records are linked to the turbine, blade, inspection date, viewing angle, and relevant operating conditions.
S447: The SCADA Gateway provides operating data that helps distinguish persistent defects from transient changes in blade appearance.
S448: The Shore Control Room monitors turbine status and records any operating restrictions required during the remote survey.
S449: A remote finding that is uncertain, growing, or potentially safety significant is referred for close-access inspection.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
